texts.preamble: M/S. Seven Star Group vs The State Of Karnataka on 28 November, 2018 Author: R Devdas Bench: R Devdas In The High Court Of Karnataka Dharwad Bench Dated This The 28Th Day Of November, 2018 Before The Hon'Ble Mr. Justice R Devdas Writ Petition No.103727/2018 (Gm-Police) Between: M/S. Seven Star Group, Plot No.1318, Auto Nagar, Kanabargi, Tq: & Dist: Belagavi, Represented By Its Acting Partner, Shri.Riyazkhan S/O Mehaboobkhan Pathan, Age: 52 Years, Occ: Business, R/O: H.No.4725, Kakar Galli, Tq & Dist: Belagavi. ... Petitioner (By Sri.V.M.Sheelavant, Advocate And Sri.Santosh B Rawoot, Advocate) And: 1. The C.P.I. Mal Maruti Police Station, Belagavi-590 016. 2. The Commissioner Of Police, Subhash Nagar, Belagavi. ... Respondents (By Smt.Veena Hegde, Aga For R1 & R2) This Writ Petition Is Filed Under Articles 226 And 227 Of The Constitution Of India Praying To Direct The Respondents To Open The Seal Put By The Respondents To Cold Storages/Business Premises Belong To Petitioner Firm Situated In Kiadb Land Bearing Plot No.1318 In Kanbargi Industrial Area, Auto Nagar, Belagavi By Hand Overing Possession Of The Above Said Cold Storage To The Petitioner. M/S. Seven Star Group vs The State Of Karnataka on 28 November, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26823982/ 1 2 This Writ Petition Coming On For Hearing On I.A., This Day, The Court Made The Following: Order
texts.facts: 2. The petitioner is a partnership firm running the business of cold storage in Plot No.1318 at Autonagar, Kanabaragi, Belagavi City in the name and style of "Seven Star Group". The petitioner is before this Court assailing the order of seizure of meat from the petitioner's premises and subjecting the same to P.F.No.30/2018 dated 01.03.2018 on the file of JMFC-II Court, Belagavi pursuant to case registration at Mal Maruti Police Station in Crime No.45/2018. 3.
texts.arguments: The learned counsel for the petitioner has produced copy of orders passed in W.P.No.102964/2018 dated 28th June, 2018 and W.P.No.102915/2018 dated 26th April, 2018. The learned counsel submits that under similar circumstances, the Co-ordinate Benches of this Court have analysed the provisions of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 and held that it is the Commissioner of Food Safety who has to decide, as per the gravity of offence, whether the matter could be referred to a Court of ordinary jurisdiction or a special Court. It was further held that it is only thereafter that criminal action for prosecution against an alleged violator of the license or regulations under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 commences.
texts.petitioner_arguments: The learned counsel for the petitioner has produced copy of orders passed in W.P.No.102964/2018 dated 28th June, 2018 and W.P.No.102915/2018 dated 26th April, 2018. The learned counsel submits that under similar circumstances, the Co-ordinate Benches of this Court have analysed the provisions of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 and held that it is the Commissioner of Food Safety who has to decide, as per the gravity of offence, whether the matter could be referred to a Court of ordinary jurisdiction or a special Court. It was further held that it is only thereafter that criminal action for prosecution against an alleged violator of the license or regulations under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 commences.
